ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the circuit diagram, the resistances are $R_1 = 2\Omega$, $R_2 = 3\Omega$, and $R_3 = 4\Omega$. 1. If the current flowing through resistor $R_1$ is known to be $I_1 = 3A$, what is the total current in the main circuit? 2. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the common node on the left is labeled A, and the common node on the right is labeled B; between the two nodes A and B there are three independent branches, and on each branch there is one resistor, labeled R1, R2, R3. Therefore, the two ends of the three resistors are connected to the same pair of nodes A and B, and they are in a parallel relationship. Reasoning: It is known that R1=2Ω, R2=3Ω, R3=4Ω. 1. If the current through R1 is I1=3A, then the common voltage of the parallel branches is V_AB=I1 R1=3×2=6V. Thus I2=V_AB/R2=6/3=2A, I3=V_AB/R3=6/4=1.5A. The total current in the main circuit is equal to the sum of the currents in each branch: I=I1+I2+I3=3+2+1.5=6.5A. 2. If the main-circuit current I=3A, first find the parallel equivalent resistance: 1/R_eq=1/2+1/3+1/4=(6+4+3)/12=13/12, so R_eq=12/13Ω. The voltage across the two ends of the parallel connection is V_AB=I R_eq=3×12/13=36/13V. The currents in each branch are: I1=V_AB/R1=(36/13)/2=18/13A, I2=V_AB/R2=(36/13)/3=12/13A, I3=V_AB/R3=(36/13)/4=9/13A.
